Use in patients receiving combined chemoradiotherapy was not recom- mended. • In patients with haematological malignancies, CSFs should be considered after induction chemotherapy in patients with acute myeloid leukaemias (patients aged over 55 may be most likely to benefit), after consolidation chemotherapy, and after initial induction or postremission chemotherapy in patients with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia; a subset of patients with myelodysplastic syndrome, severe neutropenia, and recurrent infection, might also benefit, but use in patients with refracto- ry or relapsed myeloid leukaemia was not thought to be of benefit. • CSFs were recommended as adjuncts to progenitor cell transplantation to help mobilise peripheral blood stem cells and to speed autologous engraftment. • As older patients treated with curative chemotherapy for dif- fuse aggressive lymphoma are at increased risk of febrile neu- tropenia and infections, and dose reduction strategies have been associated with a reduced response rate and survival, prophylactic CSF was recommended for such patients aged 65 and older. • Although the guidelines in adults were held to be generally applicable to children, it was noted that the potential for sec- ondary myeloid leukaemia or myelodysplastic syndrome as- sociated with CSFs was of concern in children with acute lym- phoblastic leukaemia. Guidelines issued by the US National Comprehensive Cancer Network2 adopt a similar attitude to the use of CSFs, and suggest that they should be used for prophylaxis in all patients with a more than 20% risk of febrile neutropenia or neutropenia suffi- cient to compromise treatment, and may be considered in pa- tients in whom this risk is judged to be between 10 and 20%. Factors that contribute to risk categorisation include the type of chemotherapy regimen and patient risk factors such as age, type of disease, disease stage, general health, and performance status. For details on the management of infections in neutropenic pa- tients, see Infections in Immunocompromised Patients, p.174. 1.
